gen-dafont-groovy-fs-supreme: Funky and loose, Groovy pinches its c almost shut and spreads its lowercase out, while Supreme sits crisp and heavy beside it. Supreme stays open.
gen-dafont-junegull-general-sans: Junegull has a retro swagger, pinched at every curve and tall as cast iron capitals. General Sans is the sans-serif below, with an x-height that fills the line, so give it room to breathe.
gen-dafont-stentiga-manrope: Spread-out luxury, with Stentiga's tracking opened wide and its crossbars as thick as its stems. Manrope is the friendly sans beneath, bright at every curve, so shrinking the heading would lose that grandeur.
gen-gf-autour-one-work-sans: Autour One is loud and round, with no hairline anywhere. Work Sans, the sans-serif beneath it, has a high mean line and c tips that stay apart, so it can handle a modest size.
gen-gf-funnel-display-fs-asap: Expressive spaghetti strokes give Funnel Display its voice, all one width and barely any step down from capitals to lowercase. And Asap, a sans with open arcs on its c, does the quieter job of simply being readable.
gen-gf-grandstander-fs-epilogue: Bold, constant-width lines and a tall x-height give Grandstander short ascenders and a stout look, while Epilogue draws curvy wire-thin letters in a plain sans. Their gap is the whole appeal.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-fs-merriwea: Ruler-straight strokes with ascenders that barely clear the x-height define Love Ya Like A Sister, which earns its keep big and short. Merriweather Sans follows in a sans with tall, sturdy lowercase and an e that opens clearly.
gen-gf-metamorphous-fs-public-sans: Wide sidebearings and a high midline give Metamorphous a stately, mellow look. And Public Sans, a plain sans with a hefty lowercase and broad counters, would read steadily and without fuss over pages.
gen-gf-oxanium-fs-supreme: Oxanium's tall lowercase and clean monoline strokes look like a fixed-width stencil brush. Supreme, a sans-serif with a heavy, open texture, would read crisply and firmly across a full page.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-pridi: Pridi is a serif with generous curve openings and small letters standing almost capital-sized. And New Title, with letters locked like chain links, does the bold part while Pridi keeps things refined.
